title: Happiness is…
sources: SB p.56–57 (PDF 57–58), Grammar Bank p.138–139 (PDF 139–140), Vocabulary Bank Verb forms p.158 Part 2 (PDF 159), scripts 7.8 p.122 (PDF 123); WB p.48–49 (PDF 47–48), key WB p.91–92 (PDF 91–92)

reference.title: Verbs + gerund (verb + -ing)
rows: finish
Have you finished reading the paper?
go on (= continue)
I want to go on working until I’m 70.
hate
I hate being late when I’m meeting someone.
like
I like having breakfast in a café.
love
I love waking up early on a sunny morning.
not mind
I don’t mind doing the ironing.
spend (time)
She spends hours talking on the phone.
start
It started raining at 5.30 in the morning.
stop
Please stop making such a noise.
feel like
I don’t feel like cooking today.

reference.title: start + gerund or infinitive
reference.text: After start you can use the gerund or the infinitive: It started raining. = It started to rain.

reference.title: like, love, hate
reference.text: like, love and hate are usually followed by the gerund: I love reading. After would like / would love / would hate use to + infinitive: I’d like to go.

reference.wrong: I don’t mind to do the ironing.
reference.right: I don’t mind doing the ironing.

reference.wrong: I don’t feel like to cook.

reference.title: Uses of the gerund
rows: as the subject of a sentence (like a noun)
Eating outside in the summer makes me feel good. Happiness is getting up late and not going to work.
after some verbs (love, hate, don’t mind, etc.)
I love having breakfast in bed. I hate not getting to the airport early.
after prepositions
I’m thinking of buying a new car. Jim left without saying goodbye.

reference.title: Negative gerund
reference.text: not + verb + -ing: I love not having to get up early. Happiness is not going to work.

reference.title: Spelling
reference.text: Spelling rules for the -ing form are the same as for the present continuous: live → living, stop → stopping, study → studying.

reference.wrong: Eat outside makes me feel good.
reference.right: Eating outside makes me feel good.
reference.why: As the subject of a sentence use verb + -ing.

reference.title: -ing /ɪŋ/
reference.text: The -ing ending is pronounced /ɪŋ/ (singer). Don’t pronounce a /g/ or /k/ at the end: doing /ˈduːɪŋ/, not /ˈduːɪŋk/. Compare sing /sɪŋ/ and sink /sɪŋk/.

reference.title: The letter o
reference.text: The letter o can be pronounced in many different ways: going /əʊ/, boring /ɔː/, ironing /ə/, shopping /ɒ/, doing /uː/, nothing /ʌ/.

tasks.instruction: Answer the questions about the Bank of Happiness with a partner

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). You have both listened to a radio programme about the Bank of Happiness in Tallinn: people offer services for free (English lessons, walking a dog, fixing a computer) and somebody else helps them later; nobody pays money. Ask the student: Do you think the Bank of Happiness is a good idea? Could it work in your country? Have you heard of any similar projects? Imagine you’re a member of the bank. What can you offer to do? What would you like other people to do for you? Give your own opinion briefly too (you could offer to teach guitar).
exercises.goal: Discuss the Bank of Happiness: is it a good idea, and what could you offer?
exercises.opener: So, what do you think of the Bank of Happiness? Is it a good idea?
criteria: gives an opinion about the bank with a reason
says if it could work in their country
says what they can offer to do and what they need
uses verb + -ing or to + infinitive correctly (I’m good at…, I’d like somebody to…)
